newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Ex-ally says Garang cannot win Sudanese war.
newsitem.headline: Ex-ally says Garang cannot win Sudanese war.

text.p: A rival and former ally of Sudanese rebel leader John Garang urged the veteran guerrilla fighter on Friday to abandon his campaign, saying he had no chance of a military victory.

Riek Machar, the chairman of the United Democratic Salvation Front in Sudan (UDSF) told a news conference in Harare that Garang and his Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) must join a peace agreement he and other groups had reached with the Khartoum government on April 21.

"That is the progressive way forward. The agreement is comprehensive enough to accommodate all views...whatever they are... ", he said on the sidelines of a meeting of African foreign ministers preparing for a June 2-4 summit meeting of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) in Harare.
"He cannot, because he will not be allowed to, score a military victory over the peace agreement we signed. We are waiting for him to join it," said Machar, a former lieutenant of Garang.
Officials from Garang's SPLA were not immediately available for comment.

Garang's rebel army has fought since 1983 for greater autonomy of the Christian and animist south from the Moslem, Arabised north and has launched a series of offensives this year, the most successful since 1991.
